fitSummary.roleFocus: Senior backend engineer for product teams shipping in real-world constraints
fitSummary.collaborationStyle: Works directly with product, design, and data stakeholders to scope risk-first delivery
fitSummary.timezoneOverlap: EU hours with consistent overlap for UK and US East Coast
fitSummary.availability: Open to full-time and long-term product roles

interviewPolicy.statement: I do not run trivia-based screening. I prefer real system discussion, evidence review, and tradeoff analysis.
interviewPolicy.prompt: If you want to assess me, use the artifacts below and ask how decisions were made under constraints.

seniorSignals.title: Reliability
seniorSignals.claim: I treat incidents as both response and design feedback loops.

seniorSignals.title: Performance
seniorSignals.claim: I profile bottlenecks before rewriting and optimize the highest-cost path first.

seniorSignals.title: Architecture
seniorSignals.claim: I choose service boundaries based on ownership and failure isolation, not fashion.

seniorSignals.title: Data
seniorSignals.claim: I run risky data migrations with reversible steps and production safety gates.

seniorSignals.title: Delivery
seniorSignals.claim: I ship meaningful increments while negotiating scope and timeline constraints.

seniorSignals.title: Quality
seniorSignals.claim: I design testing strategy around business risk and failure modes, not checklist coverage.

seniorSignals.title: Stakeholder Management
seniorSignals.claim: I keep delivery predictable by making decision tradeoffs explicit to non-engineering partners.

seniorSignals.title: Operations
seniorSignals.claim: I use lightweight runbooks and ownership clarity to reduce repeat production failures.

caseStudies.title: Checkout API latency and timeout recovery
caseStudies.context: Core checkout endpoint became unstable after demand spikes and regional traffic growth.
caseStudies.situation: P95 latency drifted above user tolerance during peak windows, causing timeout-related drop-off in checkout completion.
constraints: Shared database with legacy reporting workloads
Limited ability to add new infrastructure immediately
options: Rewrite checkout service end-to-end
Horizontal scale only and accept cost increase
Profile hot paths, isolate expensive query patterns, and stage targeted fixes
caseStudies.decision: Chose targeted performance work: query plan fixes, request shaping, and idempotent retry handling at failure boundaries.
tradeoffs: Did not remove all legacy coupling in phase one
Needed additional operational guardrails while rollout stabilized
caseStudies.outcome: Reduced checkout timeout rate and restored predictable peak behavior while roadmap delivery continued. Exact KPI values are confidential but were reviewed with leadership post-release.
learnings: Profiling before refactoring avoids expensive false starts
Latency and reliability should be treated as one system

caseStudies.title: Subscription domain boundary split in a live system
caseStudies.context: Monolithic subscription and billing logic slowed delivery and raised incident blast radius.
caseStudies.situation: A single service owned subscription lifecycle, invoicing logic, and partner sync integrations, creating cross-team contention.
constraints: Contract commitments tied to billing correctness
Mixed seniority engineering team and active feature pressure
options: Big-bang migration to new services
Keep monolith and patch local pain points
Incremental boundary split with compatibility layer and progressive ownership transfer
caseStudies.decision: Used incremental extraction with explicit ownership boundaries and staged read/write migration controls.
tradeoffs: Temporary duplication of logic while traffic shifted
Longer transition period to protect billing correctness
caseStudies.outcome: Delivery coordination improved across teams, incident impact scope narrowed, and new feature lead time decreased after boundary stabilization.
learnings: Boundary decisions must map to team ownership, not only technical purity
Migration safety wins over implementation speed when financial correctness is involved

decisionRecords.title: Boundary choice: orders vs payments
decisionRecords.context: Order and payment operations were tightly coupled, causing coordinated releases for unrelated changes.
decisionRecords.situation: Shared models and release pipelines increased cross-team dependency and delayed ownership.
constraints: Need to preserve existing integration contracts
options: Keep one service with modular code
Split by technical layer
Split by domain ownership with explicit API contracts
decisionRecords.decision: Separated orders and payments by business ownership with contract tests and strict dependency direction.
decisionRecords.outcome: Reduced release coupling and clearer incident ownership between domains.
learnings: Ownership boundaries should drive architecture decisions
Contract clarity matters more than internal elegance

decisionRecords.title: Migration strategy: phased writes before reads
decisionRecords.context: Critical dataset required schema evolution without downtime.
decisionRecords.situation: Legacy consumers depended on old schema assumptions while product roadmap required new structure.
options: Big-bang schema switch
Dual-read + dual-write from day one
Expand-contract with phased write/read cutover
decisionRecords.decision: Applied expand-contract pattern with validation checkpoints and rollback toggles per stage.
decisionRecords.outcome: Schema transitioned safely with controlled risk and no customer-visible outage.
learnings: Migration confidence comes from reversible steps
Operational rehearsals are part of engineering work

decisionRecords.title: Observability approach: detection tied to action
decisionRecords.context: High alert volume created fatigue, while critical regressions were still missed.
decisionRecords.situation: Monitoring existed but lacked runbook mapping and clear ownership for response.
constraints: No appetite for expensive tooling overhaul
options: Increase alerts for every known failure mode
Suppress alerts and rely on manual checks
Prioritize actionable alerting with runbook links and ownership tags
decisionRecords.decision: Implemented severity-based alerting with incident runbook linkage and post-incident prevention checkpoints.
tradeoffs: Initial tuning period with false positives
Required process consistency from engineering and product
decisionRecords.outcome: Faster incident triage and fewer repeat production issues from the same classes of failure.
learnings: Visibility without response design is noise
Incident reviews should produce concrete prevention actions

productionPatterns.title: Idempotency with bounded retries
productionPatterns.context: External dependency instability caused duplicate operations during retry storms.
productionPatterns.situation: Network and timeout errors triggered retries that sometimes repeated non-safe operations.
constraints: Business flow requires exactly-once side effects
options: Disable retries
Keep naive retries and handle duplicate cleanup manually
Apply idempotency keys, dedupe store, and bounded retry policy
productionPatterns.decision: Standardized idempotency key handling on write paths with bounded exponential retries and dead-letter escalation.
tradeoffs: Extra storage and key lifecycle management
Slight latency increase on guarded operations
productionPatterns.outcome: Reduced duplicate side effects and improved recovery behavior under transient failures.
learnings: Retries without idempotency create hidden reliability debt
productionPatterns.snippet: receive request -> check idempotency key -> if seen return prior result -> execute operation -> persist result -> ack

productionPatterns.title: Database migration safety rollout
productionPatterns.context: Business-critical table needed schema and indexing changes under active traffic.
productionPatterns.situation: Direct schema changes risked lock contention and prolonged degraded performance.
options: Single transaction migration
Pause writes during migration
Expand-contract with background backfill and staged cutover
productionPatterns.decision: Executed phased migration: additive schema, background backfill, validation checks, and controlled cutover.
tradeoffs: Need to maintain dual compatibility temporarily
productionPatterns.outcome: Delivered schema evolution without downtime and with measurable rollback safety at each phase.
productionPatterns.snippet: phase 1 add nullable columns -> phase 2 dual write -> phase 3 backfill + verify -> phase 4 switch reads -> phase 5 remove legacy fields

productionPatterns.title: Incident playbook with prevention loop
productionPatterns.context: Incident response quality varied by who was online, creating inconsistent outcomes.
productionPatterns.situation: Teams had tribal knowledge but no lightweight shared playbook for escalation and recovery.
constraints: Need to keep documentation overhead low
options: Full formal incident management rollout
Ad-hoc response only
Lightweight severity playbook with explicit ownership and post-incident actions
productionPatterns.decision: Adopted simple severity matrix, communication template, and mandatory follow-up action tracking for recurring failure classes.
tradeoffs: Requires team discipline to keep runbook current
Some edge cases still need live judgment
productionPatterns.outcome: Improved consistency in incident handling and reduced recurrence of known failure modes.
learnings: Good incident process optimizes decision quality under stress
The value is in repeatable response, not process theater
productionPatterns.snippet: detect -> triage severity -> assign incident owner -> stabilize service -> communicate status -> run post-incident review -> track prevention task

redFlags: Scope expansion without owner-level tradeoff decisions
Coverage metrics used as a proxy for product risk reduction
